newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan confirms top envoy in secret foreign visit.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan confirms top envoy in secret foreign visit.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign ministry confirmed on Tuesday foreign minister John Chang quietly left Taiwan late on Monday on a trip abroad.

"Minister Chang is out of the country. We will give more details of his visit in a few days," Chang's office told Reuters by telephone. The office declined to confirm media reports that Chang was on his way to Europe.
Chang's visit is sure to trigger angry protest from Taiwan's arch rival, China, which has viewed the island as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949.
The trip came just one day after the island severed ties with the Bahamas after learning the Caribbean nation was preparing to secure ties with Beijing.

The China Times said Chang likely will visit Brussels first and then other European countries during a visit that will last more than 10 days. The United Daily News said Chang might also visit unidentified African nations.

Now that ties with the Bahamas have been severed, Taiwan has diplomatic links with only 30 states, most of them small, poor and heavily dependent on Taipei's financial largesse. The number soon will fall to 29, as top ally South Africa has said it would switch ties in 1997.
